subject: Accelerated close playbook + AWS marketplace private offer milestones
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MAP + accelerated close proposal for AWS Marketplace private offer

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation with your ML and procurement teams, I put together an accelerated mutual action plan (MAP) and a marketplace-linked pricing staircase so your team can evaluate quickly and lock in favorable pricing via an AWS Marketplace private offer. Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestones) and a first draft of the private offer outline.

High level proposed MAP (accelerated):
- Week 0 (today): Confirm evaluation scope & procurement contacts (timothy.park@acmecorp.com?) — Redwood to provide SOC2 docs and SSO integration notes.
- Week 1 (days 1–7): 1-week pilot (customer-facing integration + 10k tokens/day smoke).
- Week 2 (days 8–14): Pilot review; success criteria call — performance, latency, cost per 1k tokens, and policy alignment.
- Week 3 (days 15–21): Execute private offer in AWS Marketplace; sign-off on commit tier to lock pricing.

Proposed MAP-linked pricing staircase (examples; finalized in private offer):
- Tier A: Immediate 6-month commit, $150k committed spend -> 10% marketplace discount + reserved capacity SLA.
- Tier B: 12-month commit, $300k committed spend -> 18% marketplace discount + priority capacity.
- Ramp/true-up: If usage exceeds committed spend, overage billed at metered rate; we offer one-time onboarding credit when customer signs private offer within 3 weeks.

Key asks from Acme to enable the accelerated close:
- Confirm procurement contact and desired legal terms for the private offer (billing entity on AWS Marketplace).
- SOC2 report request: Redwood will share the latest evidence by EOD.
- Decision cadence: can we target private-offer signature by Nov 21st?

If this timeline works I’ll schedule a short review call and loop in our Marketplace partner (Ravi) to draft the private offer.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestones), AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmecorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Park <timothy.park@acmecorp.com>, Ravi Narayanan <ravi@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + accelerated close proposal for AWS Marketplace private offer

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. The timeline looks promising — we have an upcoming procurement window on Nov 22–23, so an earlier signature would be ideal. A few clarifying Qs from our side:

- Can we compress the pilot to 3–4 days (we have a small integration sprint ready) and still keep the same pricing tiers?
- For the commit tiers, Procurement prefers net payment terms (30 days) and would like to see a sample Marketplace private offer PDF with the billing entity and order form.
- We will need SOC2 Type II and a short runbook for data residency and retention.

I’ve cc’d Timothy (procurement). We’d like to get a private offer draft in DocuSign by Friday if possible so the legal team can review ahead of the procurement window. Can Ravi help expedite the offer creation on the AWS side?

Best,
Alicia
Director of Product — Acme Corp
---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme — compress pilot & finalize commit staircase (internal)

Folks —

Alicia responded with a compressed schedule request and a procurement window. Draft answers and proposal below; please weigh in on the pricing sensitivity before I push the updated MAP back to Acme.

Summary of ask: 3–4 day pilot, private offer in DocuSign by Nov 20–21, payment terms NET30, SOC2 + data residency runbook.

Proposed adjustments (our side):
- Maintain commit tiers but add an accelerated "sign-now" incentive: if Acme signs private offer within 72 hours after pilot success, add an extra 3% one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice).
- Simplified commit staircase (definitive language for private offer):
  * Sprint Commit: 3-month minimum (pro-rated), target commitment $75k -> 8% discount.
  * Growth Commit: 6-month minimum, target $200k -> 12% discount + reserved capacity option.
  * Enterprise Commit: 12-month minimum, target $350k -> 20% discount + priority routing & dedicated support lane.
- Pricing guardrails: floor price per 1k tokens on private offers; any negotiated discount below floor requires manager approval.

Operational asks for marketplace flow (Jordan / Marcus):
- Jordan: Please confirm if AWS private offer can reflect net-30 billing to Acme, or will AWS require upfront invoice. If AWS needs a different billing flow we need to surface that to procurement ASAP.
- Marcus: confirm if we can add the one-time onboarding credit to the first invoice in our settlement flow. If not, propose an alternative (account credit applied in our billing console).

I’m planning to send the revised MAP and private offer draft back to Alicia on Friday morning. Any objections?

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Finalized accelerated-close MAP + AWS private offer draft (DocuSign link)

Hi Alicia / Timothy —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is the updated MAP (ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a polished AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf that mirrors the commit staircase we discussed. Key updates based on your notes:

- Pilot compressed to 4 days (Mon–Thu next week) with explicit success criteria (latency < 250ms p95, error rate < 0.5%, integration smoke tests pass).
- Private offer tiers adjusted: Sprint (3-month, $75k, 8%), Growth (6-month, $200k, 12%), Enterprise (12-month, $350k, 20%).
- "Sign-now" incentive: additional 3% onboarding credit if DocuSign private offer is executed within 72 hours of pilot sign-off. Credit is applied to first invoice or as an account credit (your preference noted in the DocuSign form).
- Payment terms: Draft private offer set to NET30 to match Acme’s procurement preference — Ravi, please confirm AWS Marketplace handling for NET30 billing flows.
- SOC2 & data residency runbook: attached link in DocuSign and we will also upload evidence to a secure folder by EOD.

Next steps (concise):
1) Confirm procurement billing entity and legal contact (Timothy copied).
2) Execute pilot (4 days) and confirm success criteria.
3) If pilot meets criteria, sign the DocuSign private offer: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?env=demo&token=abc123

If anything blocks the NET30 mapping on the AWS side, we’ll provide an alternative settlement arrangement and ensure it’s captured in the private offer notes.

Looking forward — can we set a 20-minute check-in after pilot day 3? I’ll invite Jordan and Marcus for any marketplace/legal clarifications.

Warmly,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
